discovery: Elucidation and direct observation of collisionless magnetic reconnection at electron scales

nominees.name: James L. Burch
nominees.affiliation: Southwest Research Institute, San Antonio, USA

nominees.name: James F. Drake
nominees.affiliation: University of Maryland, College Park, USA

motivation: Magnetic reconnection converts magnetic energy into particle energy throughout the universe, powering solar flares, magnetospheric substorms and space weather, and limiting confinement in fusion devices. For decades its rate in collisionless plasmas was a puzzle. Drake and Hesse showed theoretically and through kinetic simulation that Hall physics and non-gyrotropic electron pressure at ion and electron scales enable fast reconnection, and predicted the structure of the electron diffusion region. Burch led NASA's Magnetospheric Multiscale mission, which in 2015-2016 resolved the electron diffusion region in space for the first time and confirmed the predicted crescent-shaped electron distributions and the energy conversion there. Together, theory, simulation and in-situ measurement revealed how microscopic plasma kinetics control a fundamental process with global consequences, from Earth's magnetosphere to astrophysical plasmas.
